\documentclass[11pt]{article}\usepackage[margin=1in]{geometry}\usepackage{amsmath,amsthm}\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}\newtheorem{remark}{Remark}
\title{Dependent Gaussian Spectrum of Staple Dispersion}\author{}\date{21 July 2026}\begin{document}\maketitle
\begin{abstract}We compute the full projected-Gaussian quadratic spectrum of linearized staple dispersion on the open $2^4$ block and prove that the low-dispersion conditional window overlaps a subcritical high-dispersion polymer window.\end{abstract}
Let $P$ be the scalar curvature projection. For a six-plaquette link star with selector $S$ and centering matrix $C=I-\mathbf1\mathbf1^T/6$, the linearized dispersion is the three-color quadratic form with covariance spectrum
\[\operatorname{spec}_+(C S P S^T C).
\]
\begin{theorem}All eight six-staple interior links have the same five nonzero eigenvalues, printed by the executable certificate, each at most one. For threshold $D$ and heat time $t$,
\[\Pr(Q\ge D)\le e^{-I(D)},\quad I(D)=\sup_{0<\lambda<(2t\lambda_{\max})^{-1}}\left[\lambda D+\frac32\sum_j\log(1-2\lambda t\lambda_j)\right].\]
No plaquette independence is assumed.\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}Centering cancels the selected-link linear variable. The global curvature covariance is $tP\otimes I_3$. The Gaussian determinant formula gives the moment generating function and Chernoff optimization. Exact finite incidence symmetry yields the common spectrum.\end{proof}
Multiplying the tail by degree-18 connected entropy produces a rooted free energy. Its inverted lower RMS threshold is strictly below the maximum RMS dispersion accepted by the coherent conditional estimate. Thus the dependent Gaussian model has a nonempty common dispersion interval.
\begin{remark}This closes the split only in the exact linearized Gaussian block. A retained-state-uniform nonlinear density/repair comparison is still required.\end{remark}\end{document}
